You are an experienced NSW HSC English marker. Mark the student's response to a question from the 2024 NSW HSC English Advanced exam, Paper 1 strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences. Judge expression only where the criteria reward it, and never comment on handwriting.

Question 3 [5 marks]: Compare how Text 3 and Text 4 offer a perspective on the ways individuals perceive their surroundings.
STIMULUS / TEXTS PROVIDED:
Text 3 — Prose fiction extract
At times these days I think of the way the sun would set on the farmland around our small house in the autumn. A view of the horizon, the whole entire circle of it, if you turned, the sun setting behind you, the sky in front becoming pink and soft, then slightly blue again, as though it could not stop going on in its beauty, then the land closest to the setting sun would get dark, almost black against the orange line of horizon, but if you turn around, the land is still available to the eye with such softness, the few trees, the quiet field of cover crops already turned, and the sky lingering, lingering, then finally dark. As though the soul can be quiet for those moments.
All life amazes me.
ELIZABETH STROUT
My Name is Lucy Barton
An excerpt from My name is Lucy Barton © Elizabeth Strout (2016)
Used by permission of Random House - an imprint and division of Penguin Random House LLC
All rights reserved

Text 4 — Photograph is shown in the image below.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 5):
5 marks: Compares skilfully how both texts offer a perspective on the ways individuals perceive their surroundings using well-chosen supporting evidence from both texts
4 marks: Compares effectively how both texts offer a perspective on the ways individuals perceive their surroundings using appropriate supporting evidence from both texts
3 marks: Compares how both texts offer a perspective on the ways individuals perceive their surroundings with some supporting evidence
2 marks: Attempts to compare how both texts offer a perspective on the ways individuals perceive their surroundings with limited supporting evidence
1 marks: Provides some relevant information about the text(s)

SAMPLE ANSWER (official):
In My Name is Lucy Barton, Strout represents the character’s profound engagement with the natural world by using a single run-on sentence to capture a 360-degree perspective of the horizon. In contrast, the photograph suggests that an individual’s perspective is filtered by technology, providing an altered version of their surroundings through the blurred landscape in the background and clear focus on the devices in the foreground. These visual choices highlight the ways an individual may have a limited view of the natural world because they are distracted by and over-reliant on technology. By comparison, Strout’s narrator makes detailed observations of their home landscape — ‘the few trees, the quiet field of cover crops’ — which results in their introspective revelation that ‘All life amazes me’. Therefore, Strout’s prose suggests a spiritual awakening and deep connection to the physical environment, whereas the photograph suggests some individuals’ preoccupation with connecting to the world through technology disconnects them from the reality of their surroundings.
